name: Illustration
one_line: REFUSED. Illustration is a drawn or painted work type inside the creative default; layers, sketches, revisions, commissions, exports and rights records do not establish a separate organizational situation.
refuse_reason: Illustration fails the template node test. Its strongest signals—raster or vector artwork, layers, brushes, sketches, reference boards, same-stem revisions and rendered exports—are already the creative schema's default making-record evidence and also occur in graphic design, brand identity, game art, editorial work and motion assets. A commissioned illustration may have a brief, client correspondence, approval rounds, delivery package and licence, but those are the distinct counterparty, revision, handoff and rights workflows, not properties of illustration; the same workflows can span photography, design, copy and video. The creative placeholder declares no fields, so medium, style, subject, technique and deliverable format cannot become dimensions. Illustration therefore remains a work_type or artifact_type value under the creative default, with client-engagement, deliverable-handoff and licensing-rights handling their own situations when independently evidenced. Unreleased artwork, third-party references and licence terms remain potentially sensitive under the enclosing creative record.

deterministic: None authored for this template's activation. A readable working document with layers, brushes, artboards or a same-stem export family supports the creative schema's making record but cannot distinguish illustration from other authored visual work.

A signed commission or rights document can establish a client or licence workflow when labelled role, grant, territory or term evidence is present; it does not establish illustration as the medium of the work.
needs_llm: deciding whether a flat painted image is authored work, a downloaded reference, a portfolio case study, a stock asset or a photograph of a physical illustration
deciding whether a visual reference board and sketch set belong to one illustration brief or are a personal study unrelated to a commission
matching an untitled layered file to a named commission when only preview text, layer names and nearby correspondence overlap
deciding whether an organisation named in a brief is the commissioner, publisher, subject, depicted brand or merely a reference
deciding whether an exported PNG or PDF is an internal proof, an approved deliverable, a portfolio sample or an archive copy
deciding whether a licence or release governs the illustration itself, a reference asset, a model, a property or a downstream use
never_alone: a design_creative source type or .psd, .kra, .clip, .procreate, .ai, .svg, .tif, .png or .jpg extension; extensions route extraction and do not identify an authored illustration
the words illustration, artwork, drawing, painting, sketch, character, editorial or cover in a filename; those labels can describe a work type, reference, portfolio item or requested output
brush names, layer names, canvas dimensions, transparent background, colour profile or pixel density; these are artifact observations and do not establish a project, client or stage
a publisher, agency, brand, author or client name without labelled role-bearing text; the same name can identify commissioner, subject, licensor, maker or depicted entity
a version token such as v4, final or approved; it is universal version-family evidence and never proves approval or delivery
a single flat image, visual similarity, a shared palette or a bounded download session; each can describe a reference or unrelated image set
a maker's author metadata or a folder named Illustrations, Art or Commissions; authorship and curated vocabulary are supporting retrieval evidence, not destination facts
absence of a client; self-initiated illustration and paid illustration can share every file-format and layer signal

grouping_reasons: one named illustration or commission across sketches, working files, revisions, proofs and exports
one client engagement across multiple illustration and non-illustration outputs
one delivery or handoff set recognised by a manifest, recipient and format variants rather than by medium
one rights or release record attached to a work or reference asset without copying rights facts onto sparse images
one version family or existing curated project group, subject to P9 evidence rather than filename propagation

template.why: Empty because the creative schema declares no fields. If R1c later adopts the creative proposals such as project, stage, artifact_type and client, illustration remains a work_type or artifact_type value under that common project-first structure. A style, technique, subject, canvas size or format level would scatter one work across labels and exports; commission and rights levels belong to independently evidenced engagement and licensing workflows. Not time-first: illustration is authored work, not capture-based media.

collides_with.signal: The same rendered illustration can be a creative export or a portfolio case-study page. A case study whose purpose is demonstrating the maker's capabilities belongs to career; editable sources, proofs and delivery files remain creative. The image's illustrated content does not decide its organizational purpose.

A flat JPG or PNG may be an authored illustration, a photograph of a physical drawing, or a downloaded reference. Layer/source/export evidence supports creative making; camera capture metadata and event chronology support photos. Appearance alone cannot distinguish the records.

falls_through_to.why: A durable brief, source, release or export without recoverable creative project evidence remains an independent record.
An isolated flat image without authored-work or project evidence is not an illustration situation.
Downloaded visual studies, scans and inspiration images belong to reference material when their purpose is consumption rather than making.
Ambiguous feedback, approvals and package records require later resolution rather than a medium-based activation.

sensitivity_why: Unreleased commissions, children's or private subjects, client briefs, contact details, third-party reference assets, signed releases and licence terms may be sensitive. The protection follows the enclosing creative project, client engagement or rights record; illustration does not create a separate handling rule.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: after the creative schema receives fields, should illustration be exposed as a non-activating work_type/artifact_type or style value? Recommended: retain it as a searchable value under the creative default; do not create a medium-specific node or dimension. Separately, client commissions and rights packets should be tested by their own workflow rows rather than inferred from the word illustration.
